container.title: Containers
container.connecting: Opening a connection to the engine…
container.connectFailed: The engine could not be reached.

networks.nameInvalid: The name may use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, and must start with a letter or digit.
networks.subnetHint: Written as address/prefix — left out, the engine picks one.
networks.subnetInvalid: That is not a subnet in CIDR form: address/prefix, the prefix stopping at 32 (IPv6: at 128).
networks.gatewayHint: An address inside the subnet — left out, the engine picks the first one.
networks.gatewayInvalid: That is not an IP address.
networks.removeMessage: The network goes away. Containers still attached lose it; the engine refuses to remove a network while any are attached.
networks.none: This engine has no networks of its own to show.

compose.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or digit - the engine uses the name exactly as typed.
compose.nameInvalid: The name may use lowercase letters, digits, dashes and underscores, and must start with a letter or digit.
compose.dirHint: An absolute remote path; the Compose file is written to docker-compose.yml inside it.
compose.dirInvalid: That is not an absolute remote path.
compose.ymlHint: Checked for tab indentation and misaligned lines while it is typed; the engine reads the whole grammar.
compose.ymlTab: Line {line} indents with a tab; a Compose file indents with spaces.
compose.ymlIndent: Line {line} returns to an indentation no open level holds.
compose.startNowHint: The project is brought up detached from the file just written.
compose.none: No Compose projects on this engine yet.
compose.restartMessage: The project's containers are stopped and started again; whatever was in flight ends.
compose.downMessage: The project's containers will stop and be removed. Networks the project made go with it; volumes with names stay.
compose.upMessage: The project is brought up detached from the project's own file; the containers are created and started.

health.unhealthy: Some services are in an abnormal state.

images.showRelated: Show the containers using this image
images.tagInvalid: That is not a tag Docker would accept: letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or digit.

registry.title: Image registry
registry.failed: The engine did not answer the registry question.
registry.empty: No mirror or proxy is configured; pulls go to the upstream registry.

update.title: Update “{name}”
update.affected: {count} containers on this engine use this image. They keep running as they are; recreating one is what points it at the new image.
update.affectedNone: No container on this engine uses this image.
update.dataRisk: A container's data lives in its volumes and writable layers, not in the image: pulling a newer image removes nothing. Recreating a container is the step that can affect what it holds.
update.sourceLead: The pull will go where this daemon sends its pulls:
update.sourceFailed: The daemon did not answer the registry question.
update.sourceNone: No mirror is configured; the pull goes to the upstream registry.
update.committing: Confirming closes this dialog and starts the pull in the task panel — this dialog no longer waits and cannot undo it. An update already running for this image is not started a second time.
update.failure: If the pull fails, the task panel keeps the reason and the log to read, retry, or stop; the image on this engine is left exactly as it is.

container.filesFailed: Could not open the files of {name}: {reason}

filters.text: Filter by name, image or ID

confirm.stopMessage: Its processes end now. The container stays in the list, stopped, and can be started again.
confirm.restartMessage: Its processes end and start again from the same image and configuration.
confirm.removeMessage: The container and its writable layer are deleted. Images and named volumes it used are kept.
confirm.dataLoss: All data inside the container will be lost.

create.title: New container
create.name: Name
create.portInvalid: Ports are whole numbers, and a row needs both sides.
create.volumeInvalid: A volume is written as “host path:container path”.
create.terminalHint: Both are needed for a container that will be entered with a shell.

wizard.title: New container wizard
wizard.imageHint: Written as name:tag — the tag may be left out.
wizard.nameHint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, at most 64 characters; left empty, the engine names it.
wizard.nameInvalid: The name may use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, must start with a letter or digit, and stops at 64 characters.
wizard.autostartHint: The engine starts the container again whenever the engine starts.
wizard.privilegedWarning: The container may do anything to the host. Only for images you trust.
wizard.portInvalid: Ports are whole numbers between 1 and 65535, and a row needs both sides.
wizard.portDuplicate: Host port {port} ({protocol}) is listed more than once.
wizard.volumeInvalid: A volume row needs a host path and a container path.
wizard.envInvalid: A variable needs a key, and the key may not contain “=”.
wizard.labelInvalid: A label needs a name, and the name may not contain “=”.
wizard.memoryInvalid: The limit is a whole number of megabytes.
wizard.commandHint: One line, split on spaces — no shell.

commit.title: Commit as an image
commit.author: Author
commit.hint: The container is not touched: its file system is written into a new image.

logs.title: Logs of {name}
logs.noErrors: No line reads as an error.
logs.paused: Paused — lines are kept and appear when resumed.

image.loadTitle: Load an image from an archive
image.pruneMessage: Every image not used by a container is deleted. This cannot be undone.
image.removeMessage: The image is deleted. Containers made from it keep running.
